mission_objective: First crewed lunar landing; crew EVA, sample collection, instrument deployment
scientific_contribution: First humans on the Moon; collected 21.5 kg lunar samples; deployed PSEP seismic experiment
verification_notes: Coordinates verified from NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter LROC image M175124933L; source: https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/383

mission_objective: Detect moonquakes and meteorite impacts on lunar surface
scientific_contribution: Recorded first lunar seismic data; operated 21 days before power failure

mission_objective: Reflect laser pulses from Earth to measure Earth-Moon distance precisely
scientific_contribution: Ongoing measurement of Earth-Moon distance; confirms lunar recession rate ~3.8 cm/year; tests General Relativity
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 1969-059C-05; still used by observatories worldwide as of 2024

mission_objective: Second crewed lunar landing; precision landing near Surveyor 3; sample collection
scientific_contribution: Landed 155 m from Surveyor 3; crew retrieved Surveyor 3 camera; collected 34.4 kg samples
verification_notes: Coordinates from NASA LROC image; source: https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/231

mission_objective: Soft landing; test soil mechanics; photograph lunar surface for Apollo site selection
scientific_contribution: Returned 6315 images; soil bearing tests; camera retrieved by Apollo 12 crew in 1969 — unique returned artifact
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 1967-035A; camera returned to Earth; lander remains on surface; coordinates from LROC

equipment_name: Apollo 12 Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP)
mission_objective: Deploy seismic, magnetometer, solar wind and atmosphere experiments
scientific_contribution: Returned continuous scientific data for ~7.5 years; seismic data revealed lunar interior layering
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 1969-099C; NASA terminated all ALSEP stations 1977-09-30 to save DSN costs

mission_objective: Third crewed lunar landing in Fra Mauro formation; sample collection from Imbrium ejecta
scientific_contribution: Collected 42.6 kg samples from Fra Mauro; first use of Modular Equipment Transporter (MET) pull-cart
verification_notes: Coordinates from LROC NAC image M168000580LR; source: https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/397

mission_objective: Provide second Earth-Moon laser ranging station to improve measurement geometry
scientific_contribution: Provides second data point for LLR studies; combined with Apollo 11 and 15 LRRRs enables 3-point baseline
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 1971-008C-05; active as of 2024

equipment_name: Apollo 14 Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP)
mission_objective: Deploy seismic, ionosphere, charged particle and heat flow experiments
scientific_contribution: Seismic data revealed deep moonquakes; heat flow measurements gave lunar thermal gradient data
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 1971-008C; terminated 1977-09-30

mission_objective: First J-mission extended landing; Hadley Rille geology; first Lunar Roving Vehicle deployment
scientific_contribution: Collected 76.8 kg samples including genesis rock (anorthosite); first orbital subsatellite deployed
verification_notes: Coordinates from LROC NAC image M113751661L; source: https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/231

mission_objective: First crewed lunar rover; extend crew range from lander; geological traverse
scientific_contribution: Traversed 27.9 km total; allowed sampling at Hadley Rille and Apennine Front impossible on foot
verification_notes: LRV parked ~91 m from LM; distance from LROC imagery; total traverse from NASA mission report

mission_objective: Provide third and largest LLR station; improve ranging accuracy
scientific_contribution: Largest array (300 corner cubes vs 100 on Apollo 11/14); provides highest signal return; still in use 2024
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 1971-063A-07; active as of 2024; McDonald Observatory and others range it regularly

equipment_name: Apollo 15 Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP)
mission_objective: Deploy heat flow, seismic, magnetometer and solar wind experiments
scientific_contribution: First successful heat flow measurement on Moon; lunar surface magnetism data; seismic network with Apollo 12 and 14
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 1971-063A; terminated 1977-09-30

mission_objective: Highland geology; Descartes formation sampling; ultraviolet astronomy from lunar surface
scientific_contribution: Collected 95.8 kg samples (most of any mission); first astronomical UV camera on Moon; Descartes not volcanic as expected
verification_notes: Coordinates from LROC image; source: https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/231

mission_objective: Extend crew geological traverse range in Descartes Highlands
scientific_contribution: Traversed 26.7 km; reached Stone Mountain and North Ray Crater; samples showed highland crust formation
verification_notes: Total traverse distance from NASA mission report JSC-07904

equipment_name: Apollo 16 Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP)
mission_objective: Cosmic ray, seismic, magnetometer and passive seismic experiments
scientific_contribution: Lunar magnetic anomaly data; cosmic ray detector results contributed to solar wind studies
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 1972-031A; terminated 1977-09-30

mission_objective: Final Apollo mission; Taurus-Littrow valley; first geologist astronaut on Moon (Schmitt)
scientific_contribution: Collected 110.5 kg samples (highest of any mission); orange soil discovery indicated ancient volcanic activity
verification_notes: Coordinates from LROC NAC image M104318871LR; source: https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/231

mission_objective: Geological traverses across Taurus-Littrow valley including North and South Massif
scientific_contribution: Traversed 35.9 km (longest LRV traverse); TV camera left running to film LM ascent stage liftoff
verification_notes: Traverse distance from NASA mission report; LRV parked SE of LM

equipment_name: Apollo 17 Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP)
mission_objective: Seismic profiling, heat flow, atmospheric and gravitational wave experiments
scientific_contribution: Provided seismic data for final network dataset; heat flow measurements; terminated with all ALSEP stations 1977
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 1972-096A; terminated 1977-09-30

mission_objective: First US soft landing on Moon; demonstrate landing technology; photograph surface
scientific_contribution: Returned 11237 images; confirmed surface can support Apollo lander weight; pioneered US soft landing
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 1966-045A; last contact 1966-07-14

mission_objective: Soil chemistry analysis; first alpha-scattering surface analysis on Moon
scientific_contribution: First in-situ chemical analysis of lunar soil; confirmed basaltic composition of Mare Tranquillitatis
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 1967-083A; landed 2.5 km from future Apollo 11 site

mission_objective: Soil mechanics; first spacecraft to lift off from lunar surface (vernier engine test)
scientific_contribution: Only spacecraft to lift off and re-land on Moon; soil chemistry data for Sinus Medii region
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 1967-112A; lifted off 2.4 m and re-landed 1967-11-17

mission_objective: First highland landing; soil chemistry at Tycho crater rim ejecta
scientific_contribution: Returned 21091 images; alpha-scatter analysis of highland soil; distinctly different from mare sites
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 1968-001A; last contact 1968-02-21

mission_objective: First successful Mars landing; biology experiments; weather monitoring; surface imaging
scientific_contribution: First clear images of Mars surface; first biology experiments (inconclusive); 6 years of weather data; first Mars meteorology
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 1975-075C; contact lost 1982-11-13 after software error; coordinates from NASA Viking site

mission_objective: Second Mars lander; biology and seismic experiments at higher latitude site
scientific_contribution: First images from Utopia Planitia; first Mars seismometer data (inconclusive — instrument on lander not surface); water frost observed
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 1975-083C; contact lost 1980-04-11 after battery failure; coordinates from NASA

equipment_name: Mars Pathfinder Lander (Carl Sagan Memorial Station)
mission_objective: Demonstrate low-cost Mars landing; deploy first Mars rover (Sojourner); atmospheric and soil studies
scientific_contribution: Returned 16500+ images; confirmed conglomerate rocks indicating past water flows; proved airbag landing system
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 1996-068A; last contact 1997-09-27; renamed Carl Sagan Memorial Station

mission_objective: First Mars rover; demonstrate rover mobility; APXS chemical analysis of rocks
scientific_contribution: Analyzed 16 rocks and soils; confirmed basaltic composition; operated 83 sols (planned 7); 100 m traverse
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 1996-068B; last contact via lander 1997-09-27; 83 sols operation confirmed by NASA JPL

mission_objective: Geological investigation of Gusev Crater as possible ancient lake bed
scientific_contribution: Discovered silica-rich soil indicating past hydrothermal activity; 7.73 km total traverse; operated 2208 sols (planned 90)
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 2003-032A; last contact 2010-03-22; declared mission end 2011-05-25; coordinates from NASA MER site

mission_objective: Geological investigation of Meridiani Planum; search for past water evidence
scientific_contribution: Found hematite concretions (blueberries) proving past liquid water; 45.16 km traverse (Mars distance record); 5111 sols
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 2003-032B; last contact 2018-06-10 during planet-wide dust storm; 45.16 km traverse confirmed by NASA

mission_objective: Investigate habitability of arctic Mars soil; detect water ice; study climate
scientific_contribution: Confirmed water ice in Martian soil; observed snowfall; detected perchlorate salts affecting habitability assessment
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 2007-034A; last contact 2008-11-02; coordinates from NASA Phoenix site; ice confirmed by TEGA instrument

mission_objective: Study Mars interior structure using seismometer; measure heat flow; detect marsquakes
scientific_contribution: Recorded 1319 marsquakes; revealed Mars has a liquid outer core; detected meteorite impacts seismically; first planetary interior seismology
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 2018-042A; declared end of mission 2022-12-21; 1319 marsquakes from final NASA report; coordinates confirmed

mission_objective: First powered controlled flight on another planet; scout for Perseverance rover
scientific_contribution: Completed 72 flights; first powered flight on Mars 2021-04-19; proved aerial reconnaissance concept; total 17 km flight distance
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 2020-052B; rotor blade damaged flight 72 on 2024-01-18; declared end 2024-01-25; 72 flights confirmed

equipment_name: MSL Curiosity Rover Sky Crane / Descent Stage
mission_objective: Deliver Curiosity rover safely to Gale Crater surface using Sky Crane maneuver
scientific_contribution: Proved Sky Crane EDL concept enabling landing of heavy rovers; crash-landed ~650 m from Curiosity after delivery
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 2011-070A; crash site imaged by MRO HiRISE; approximate coordinates; exact position from HiRISE image ESP_028401_1750

mission_objective: Deliver Perseverance rover to Jezero Crater using Sky Crane system
scientific_contribution: Demonstrated improved EDL with Terrain Relative Navigation; crash site imaged by Perseverance cameras
verification_notes: NSSDCA ID: 2020-052A; crash site photographed by Perseverance Mastcam-Z; Terrain Relative Navigation first use confirmed

mission_objective: Protect Curiosity during Mars atmospheric entry
scientific_contribution: Largest heat shield used at Mars (4.5 m diameter); imaged on surface by Curiosity; thermal protection data improved future EDL designs
verification_notes: Imaged on surface by Curiosity sol 14 (2012-08-21); coordinates approximate from HiRISE imagery
